Triangle versus linear-decrease EEG decoding

The classifier predicts the delivered waveform, Triangle (241) or LinDec (242). Each participant and presentation position has its own model. Entire waveform-comparison groups are held out.

Research question and origin

Collu et al. reported 70% median behavioral match-to-sample discrimination of triangle versus linear decrease under matched charge and peak current. WD-009 asks whether the delivered waveforms can also be distinguished from EEG. The targets come from verified triggers. Collu et al.

Experimental settings and filters

Target: distinguish Triangle from LinDec using individual Task 4 EEG epochs. Models are fitted separately for each participant and first/second presentation; entire comparison blocks are held out.

Nominal charge: the default includes participants 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10, whose Triangle and LinDec settings give equal nominal charge (247 epochs). The other five participants have different waveform-specific amplitudes and are included when selecting “All charge settings” (501 epochs). Charge is never a model input.

Comparison context: “All waveform pairs” includes every eligible Triangle or LinDec epoch, whether paired with each other or with Sine, Square or linear increase. “Direct pairs” includes only Triangle–LinDec comparisons (126 epochs; 66 with matched charge). “Other pairs” excludes those direct comparisons (375 epochs; 181 with matched charge). Each filter summarizes saved held-out predictions without retraining.

Presentation: first and second pulses are evaluated separately. The participant selector changes the tables; cohort plots always show all participants eligible for the chosen filters.

BA is balanced accuracy, the mean of the two waveform recalls, with a 50% reference. Participant means weight participants equally. Charge and context filters select existing held-out predictions; they do not refit the models. Post − pre is a paired difference in percentage points (pp). Intervals and p-values apply to participant means; an individual selection shows its difference only.

Cohort plots

These plots follow the selected evaluation subset and presentation. Tables above can select an individual participant.

Significance test

For each configuration, count participants whose post BA exceeds pre BA and whose post BA is lower; ties are omitted. The exact two-sided sign test asks whether improvements and decreases are equally likely across independent participants. It tests consistency of the direction of change, not its magnitude or individual decoding above chance. Holm correction covers all 72 comparisons: six configurations × six filter subsets × two positions. With only five non-tied participants, even five improvements give a two-sided p of 0.0625.

Exact binomial test · Holm correction.

Epoch and charge coverage

The table shows why only five participants qualify for charge matching. Counts combine both presentation positions and all waveform-pair blocks. The filters above then select the desired epochs. Trial counts vary because each Task 4 comparison stops when one waveform receives five votes.

Nominal cathodic charge is peak amplitude × 0.4 ms × 0.5 for both Triangle and LinDec. Their shape factors are equal, but threshold amplitudes vary by participant and waveform. These are documented nominal settings; current-monitor measurements remain unavailable.

Features and models

Voltage features

All 62 electrodes contribute voltage means in 50 or 100 ms bins. Post EEG spans 50–1,050 ms; pre EEG spans −1,050 to −50 ms. This gives 1,240 or 620 original features.

Reference and baseline

A common pair baseline measured −1,250 to −1,050 ms before the first pulse is subtracted from all windows. Processing uses the instantaneous 62-channel average reference, without temporal filtering or ICA.

PCA

Feature scaling and principal component analysis are fitted on the training fold. PCA retains components accounting for 90% of training variance and transforms the held-out epochs using that fitted basis.

Shrinkage LDA

Linear discriminant analysis uses automatic covariance shrinkage and equal class priors, with PCA-reduced features as its input.

Linear SVM

The support vector machine uses a linear kernel, fixed C=1 and balanced class weights. It is evaluated both with PCA-reduced features and with the original scaled voltage features.

Validation

Within each participant and presentation, training excludes the entire held-out comparison. For a direct triangle/LinDec block, the model learns from triangle and LinDec presentations paired with other waveforms. All scaling and dimension reduction use training data only.

Interpretation

First-presentation performance is the primary view. Second-presentation pre and post EEG can contain effects of the preceding pulse. The WD-008 behavioral order audit identifies an association between choices and order, without establishing physiological carryover or showing that second presentations are unusable.

The first-pulse EEG window ends before the second pulse, so a direct pair is optional for that analysis. Comparison blocks can still differ in expectation and recording order. For the second pulse, pair context also changes which waveform preceded the epoch. Whole-comparison-group validation addresses shared block context.

All-channel finite values and fixed original complete-pair QC are checked. Additional channels have descriptive amplitude flags. The intervals resample participants conditional on fixed held-out predictions. Sign tests compare post with pre across participants; no refitted label-permutation test of above-chance decoding is included. Physical delivery and response timing remain unverified.
